note: The statement-parity oracle. Each pipeline is translated with
translateStatement and run against the fixture, and evaluated by SEL over
the same rows loaded as the relation; the two row sets must match, value
for value. Unless a statement says "ordered", rows are compared as a set,
because a statement without an ORDER BY promises no order.
rows.json asks about WHERE clauses; this asks about the statement compiler:
GROUP BY, HAVING, ORDER BY, LIMIT, derived tables. It exists because the
sql/cases strings were byte-identical in every host while MariaDB merged
'A' and 'a' into one group (review 2026-09-15 finding L): only a server
can say whether GROUP BY means what BUCKET means.
Numbers are compared as numbers (COUNT comes back as an int here and a
string there); everything else byte for byte.

context.query: SELECT id, cat, v FROM grp_items ORDER BY id

statements.name: numeric grouped values keep numeric order across a derived table
statements.sel: ITEMS .> BUCKET(_["v"], RECORD("v", _K, "n", COUNT(_))) .> TAKE(100) .> SORT_BY(_["v"])

statements.name: numeric group preserves input text and numeric ordering
bounded slice mixed
statements.sel: ITEMS .> SORT_BY(_["id"]) .> DROP(1) .> TAKE(2) .> DROP(1) .> TAKE(3) .> MAP(RECORD("id", _["id"]))

statements.name: bounded slice filter
statements.why: The direct id column retains its NUM declaration through the bounded derived slice, including on SQLite.
statements.sel: ITEMS .> SORT_BY(_["id"]) .> TAKE(2) .> DROP(1) .> FILTER(_["id"] > 0) .> MAP(RECORD("id", _["id"]))

statements.name: bounded slice bucket
statements.sel: ITEMS .> SORT_BY(_["id"]) .> TAKE(2) .> DROP(1) .> BUCKET(_["cat"], RECORD("cat", _K, "n", COUNT(_)))

statements.name: bounded slice empty-input
statements.sel: ITEMS .> SORT_BY(_["id"]) .> TAKE(0) .> TAKE(2) .> DROP(1) .> MAP(RECORD("id", _["id"]))

statements.name: bare bucket keys are the exact bytes
sort by a text key is byte order
sort by a text key, descending
filter after pagination is a where over the paginated groups
statements.sel: ITEMS .> BUCKET(_["cat"], RECORD("cat", _K, "n", COUNT(_))) .> SORT_BY(_["cat"]) .> TAKE(2) .> FILTER(_["n"] > 1)
statements.why: sqlite has no way to ask whether the derived n is a number, so the FILTER over it is refused there

statements.name: text equality in a where is the control
